learning_objective: 🎯 Get introduced to the main Taals in the syllabus! Memorize the Thekas of Teentaal, Dadra, Keherwa, and learn how to write them in different speeds (Single, Double, Quadruple).

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: आवर्तन (One complete cycle of a Taal)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: When exactly one syllable (Bol) is spoken or played per beat (Matra), it is called 'Thah' or Ekgun. This establishes the original, foundational tempo of the Taal.

When two syllables are spoken or played within the time of a single beat, it is called Dugun. In written notation, an underline (crescent) is drawn below the two bols (e.g., <u>Dha Dhin</u>) to show they share one beat. The speed doubles!
When four syllables are squeezed into the time of a single beat, it is called Chaugun (e.g., <u>Dha Dhin Dhin Dha</u>). The speed becomes four times as fast as the original Thah.
A 6-beat cycle. 2 Vibhags of 3 beats each. Sam (X) is on the 1st beat, Khali (0) is on the 4th beat. Theka: Dha Dhi Na | Dha Ti Na.
An 8-beat cycle. 2 Vibhags of 4 beats each. Sam (X) is on the 1st beat, Khali (0) is on the 5th beat. Theka: Dha Ge Na Ti | Na Ka Dhi Na.
A 16-beat cycle. 4 Vibhags of 4 beats each. It has 3 Taalis (on beats 1, 5, 13) and 1 Khali (on the 9th beat). Theka: Dha Dhin Dhin Dha | Dha Dhin Dhin Dha | Dha Tin Tin Ta | Ta Dhin Dhin Dha.

fun_activity.title: 👏 The Taali-Khali Game
fun_activity.instructions: Try 'playing' Teentaal (16 beats) on your hands. Clap loudly on the 1st, 5th, and 13th beats. On the 9th beat, wave your hand silently outward in the air (Khali). Keep counting steadily from 1 to 16 out loud while doing this!

exam_tips: 📌 You must know how to write Taal notation using the Bhatkhande Notation System. Never forget to mark the Vibhag lines (|) and the symbols for Sam (X) and Khali (0).
📌 Check your math carefully when writing Dugun or Chaugun. For example, a 16-beat Chaugun of Teentaal must perfectly fit into just 4 actual beats!
📌 Writing the Dugun notation of Dadra or Keherwa is a very common, straightforward 3 or 4-mark question in exams.
quick_recap: ⭐ Dadra (6 beats) is the most widely used Taal in light music, ghazals, and bhajans.
⭐ Teentaal (16 beats) is considered the 'King' of Taals; classical music training almost always begins with it.
